papers.title: Iliac fossa block is useful for postoperative analgesia of total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background: Benefit of combined regional anesthesia during lower-extremity joint operation under general anesthesia have been reported. However, a peripheral nerve block presents a risk of nerve injury. Here we examined new type of block; iliac fossa block, in which a medicinal solution is injected into the iliac fossa distant from the nerve. Like a conventional fascia iliaca compartment block, the iliac fossa block can block the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve, the femoral nerve and the obturator nerve. In addition, because of the local anesthetic spread to the central side, the block can be expected to act on the lumbar plexus.Methods: This study was approved by the Ethics Committee, and we informed consent from adult patients who were confirmed to undergo a total hip arthroplasty (THA) under general anesthesia. Patients who were contraindicated for regional anesthesia or had neurological disorders, diabetes mellitus, etc. were excluded. Although the securing of airway and the medication for general anesthesia were at the discretion of each anesthesiologist, fentanyl and remifentanil were used as opioids. In the iliac fossa block group after the induction of anesthesia, 40 ml of 0.25% ropivacaine was injected, in the control group, the block was not used. We determined the amount of fentanyl used during each surgery and the requirements of fentanyl as intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (IV-PCA) up to 48 hr post-surgery. The primary outcome was cumulative fentanyl requirements up to 48 hr post-surgery. We also checked the block area by cold test. The values were mean u00b1 standard deviation, p value less than 0.05 was considered as significant in the unpaired t-test and Chi-squared test . Results: Age and BMI average were 60 years old and 24 kg / m 2, respectively, with no significant difference between the two groups. In regarding to intraoperative fentanyl dose, there was no significant difference between 208 u00b1 80 u00b5g in the block group (n = 10) and 242 u00b1 61 u00b5g in the control group (n = 13). The cumulative fentanyl requirements at 24 h postoperatively were significantly less in Group B than Group C; 274 u00b1 46 u03bcg vs. 468 u00b1 305 u03bcg (p = 0.03), at 48 h were no significant difference; 557 u00b1 138 u03bcg vs. 788 u00b1 405 u03bcg (p = 0.05) The surgical time was significantly longer in the block group (p=0.01).Conclusion: The postoperative fentanyl requirements were significantly less in the iliac fossa block group, and this block was useful for the postoperative analgesia of THA.

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the analgesic efficacy of iliac fossa block for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A controlled trial comparing fentanyl consumption during and after surgery between patients receiving iliac fossa block and those receiving no block.
summary_en.result: The iliac fossa block group had significantly lower cumulative fentanyl requirements at 24 hours post-surgery, but no significant difference at 48 hours.
summary_en.validation: The block effect was assessed by cold testing, and statistical comparisons were made using t-test and chi-squared test.

papers.title: Three-dimensional bioprinting in dermatology
papers.abstract:
Three-dimensional (3D) printing is a new digital forming technology based on computed 3D digital imaging and multi-level continuous printing. 3D bioprinting is based on the 3D printing technology, and uses living cells as biological materials to print living tissues or organs. In recent years, 3D bioprinting has been applied in clinic more and more widely, e.g., in vitro regeneration and reconstruction of the skin, bones, blood vessels, cardiac tissues, and so on. Currently, many skin diseases such as vitiligo and psoriasis are very difficult to treat, which have become research hotspots and challenges in the dermatological field. 3D bioprinting technology can be applied to researches of skin diseases and skin wound repair, and has brought a new dawn for patients with skin diseases.


Key words: 
Skin diseases; Skin; Imaging, three-dimensional; Concept formation; 3D bioprinting

llm.why_not_core: No AI integration in bioprinting workflow, no experimental validation, and no autonomous decision-making; purely a clinical review.

summary_zh.method: 归纳近年来相关文献，总结3D生物打印在皮肤再生与疾病研究中的应用。
summary_zh.result: 3D生物打印为皮肤疾病治疗提供了新途径。
summary_zh.validation: 综述性质，无具体实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: This review aims to summarize the current applications and future potential of three-dimensional bioprinting in dermatology.
summary_en.method: The study systematically reviews recent literature on 3D bioprinting techniques for skin tissue engineering and disease modeling.
summary_en.result: 3D bioprinting offers promising approaches for skin wound repair and studying skin diseases such as vitiligo and psoriasis.
summary_en.validation: No original experimental validation; the paper is a literature review.
